title: Director of Expeditions
description:
Director of Expeditions - School in Switzerland

A prestigious and internationally renowned boarding school in Switzerland is seeking an outstanding Director of Expeditions to lead one of the most distinctive outdoor education programmes in the world. Reporting to a senior member of the leadership team, the successful candidate will provide strategic and operational leadership for a large-scale expedition programme encompassing mountain, ski and adventure-based learning experiences. This is a rare opportunity for an experienced outdoor education professional with strong leadership credentials, technical expertise in alpine environments and a passion for developing young people through challenge, resilience and discovery.

JOB PURPOSE
The Director of Expeditions serves as the strategic lead for Aiglon’s renowned expedition department. The post holder is responsible for the development and delivery of the programme’s vision and ethos, ensuring it is progressive, relevant, and distilled into a coherent curriculum across the whole school. They provide leadership to a team of qualified expeditioners and ensure that all activities are managed with the highest standards of safety and risk management.
KEY TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THE POSITION

1. Strategic Leadership & Vision

Visionary Design: Develop and oversee the philosophy and approach of our expedition programme, ensuring it reflects our aim to continue to be world leading in outdoor pursuit provision.
Curriculum Development: Develop and implement the expedition programme ensuring it is progressive for all students, regardless of age or length of stay at Aiglon.
Challenge: Ensure challenge is appropriate to ability and context, acknowledging that expeditions serve pastoral and community-building purposes alongside physical stretch.
Reinforce the purpose of expeditions: independence, resilience, responsibility and growth.
Holistic Assessment: Take a lead role in the school’s development of holistic assessment within the expedition context.
External Engagement: Seek to build relationships with the wider community to share expertise and gain insights from external best practices, with particular emphasis on risk management.

2. Operational Oversight & Management
Team Leadership: Provide instruction and guidance to the Head of Senior and Junior Expeditions in their operational oversight.
Leadership: Provide inspiration, leadership and guidance to all teaching staff involved in expeditions with the expectation to deliver the highest standards and professionalism.
Staff Development: Manage professional reviews, appraisals, and training (internal and external) for the expedition staff.
Meetings: Chair expedition department meetings and work closely with both Junior and Senior heads to ensure departmental alignment.
Stakeholder Liaison: Liaise with the School Council, Assistant Heads, Houseparents, and academic departments.
Recruitment: Oversee and support the recruitment of all expedition staff, including guides.
Development: Monitor and continually improve the process of student reflection.
Administration: Ensure all paperwork and communication is complete, efficient and effective.
Budgets: Preparation and management of all Expedition budgets
Administration: Use Aiglon’s data management system to record and organise all expeditions
Mountain School: Line-manage the Junior Mountain School Programme, with specific liaison with the Bear Grylls Survival Academy
Summer Camp: Act as the senior advisor for all summer expedition activities, ensuring a robust handover of safety protocols and operational standards to the Summer School team while maintaining ultimate accountability for safeguarding and risk management frameworks.
3. Safety, Risk & Compliance
Safety Evaluation: Oversee and evaluate the safety protocols of the entire expedition programme.
Risk Management: Encourage and verify a high level of risk management documentation and ensure operating standards align with best practice.
Open Culture: Ensure a safe and open environment for staff to share experiences and opinions to improve safety.
Compliance: Ensure that all equipment and its usage comply with current PPE and safety standards.
Work closely with the HR team and Director of Compliance to ensure compliance with all necessary processes relating to recruitment of guides.
Ensure that qualifications of all staff and Guides are appropriate.
Safeguarding: Ensure all staff and Guides receive safeguarding training at regular intervals. There is an expectation to uphold the highest standards of safeguarding.

4. Logistics & Equipment Management
Planning & Bookings: Oversee and guide administrative support and the Heads of Expeditions to ensure bookings are made with a nine to twelve-month lead-in.
Stores Management: Manage the expedition stores, including the upkeep, care, and long-term planning for equipment.
Inventory Systems: Manage robust systems for recording inventories and maintenance schedules.
5. Communication & Ethos
Internal Communication: Ensure students, staff and parents receive effective and efficient information regarding upcoming expeditions through assemblies, staff meetings, bulletins and external communication.
External Communication: Work with communications, admissions, and advancement teams to ensure clear and inspiring messaging to the wider community, that is delivered to a high professional standard..
Institutional Values: Contribute enthusiastically to the life and work of the school, upholding the Aiglon ethos, including the delivery of meditations.
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
The Director of Expeditions is expected to be visible and motivational presence and contribute to the overall life of the Aiglon community
Undertake additional responsibilities as may arise at the reasonable request of the Director of Character Education and the Director of School.

The qualifications, experiences and attributes of the post holder must match the detailed specification below:
A. Education, Qualifications and Languages
Essential

Swiss-recognised International Mountain Leader/Accompagnateur
Winter mountaineering or ski qualification
Rock Climbing Instructor
First Aid certification
Driving licence
Professional working proficiency in French and a fluency in English

Desirable

Teaching qualification
Holder of an IFGMA qualification
Higher level qualification in other adventure activities:
Paddlesports
Mountain Biking

B. Experience and Knowledge
Essential

Experience in health and safety auditing, incident management protocols, and Swiss legal requirements for high-risk activities.
Experience in managing department budgets, equipment procurement, and overseeing a team of full-time and freelance staff.
Experience in designing progressive outdoor education programs that align with educational frameworks
Experience leading and teaching young people and groups in the European mountains in a variety of adventurous activities
Highly competent skier
Professional-level competence in winter navigation and avalanche safety
Experience in the creation and delivery of presentations and information to a wide range of audiences

C. Personal Qualities, Attitudes and Behaviours
Essential

Ability to build professional relationships with students within the clear boundaries of Aiglon’s safeguarding policies.
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively across all stakeholders.
The ability to inspire confidence in staff, students and parents whilst articulating the value of risk to the School Council and Board of Directors.
Proven ability to remain calm and lead a team through high-pressure emergency situations in remote environments.
Aiglon expects the Director to have a commitment to continuous professional development, staying at the forefront of international outdoor education trends and safety standards; they should also be expected to mentor junior staff in their professional development.

title: Export Compliance Engineer

- Zudem: Durchführung ärztlicher Verordnungen sowie sichere Abgabe der Medikamente
- Zudem überwachen Sie die Vitalzeichen, denn Sie erkennen früh, wenn sich etwas ändert

- Zuerst das Fachliche: die Ausbildung als dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF oder FH
- Bei ausländischem Diplom: SRK-Anerkennung zwingend erforderlich
- Zudem Erfahrung in der Langzeitpflege, Akutpflege oder Reha
- Vor allem Verantwortung, Empathie sowie eine belastbare, ruhige Art

Sie arbeiten in einem betreuten Wohnumfeld: Alltag gestalten, begleiten, fördern. Hier zählt die Beziehung ebenso wie die Pflege, denn Lebensqualität entsteht aus beidem. Ein Umfeld für Menschen, die gerne ganzheitlich arbeiten.

Kurz gesagt: Als Pflegefachfrau HF/FH Betreuung in Seedorf verbinden Sie Fachlichkeit mit einem Umfeld, das zu Ihnen passt. Genau solche Stellen vermitteln wir am liebsten.

### Der Beruf im Detail: Was macht eine diplomierte Pflegefachperson HF/FH?

Als diplomierte Pflegefachperson HF/FH tragen Sie die fachliche Verantwortung über den ganzen Pflegeprozess. Sie erheben den Pflegebedarf, danach planen Sie die Massnahmen und werten die Ergebnisse aus. Zudem steuern Sie die Abgabe der Medikamente, überwachen Vitalzeichen und erkennen Veränderungen früh. Damit sichern Sie Tag für Tag die Qualität der Pflege.

Der Weg in diesen Beruf führt über die höhere Fachschule (HF) oder das Bachelorstudium Pflege (FH). Ausländische Diplome brauchen dafür eine [Anerkennung durch das Schweizerische Rote Kreuz (SRK)](https://www.redcross.ch/de/srk-anerkennung). Ausserdem stehen erfahrenen Fachpersonen viele Wege offen: ein Nachdiplomstudium (NDS), die Rolle als Berufsbildnerin oder die Teamleitung.

Der Arbeitsmarkt für Pflegefachfachpersonen im Kanton Bern zeigt eine stabile Nachfrage nach qualifizierten Fachkräften. In der Region Seedorf finden Sie attraktive Positionen in Spitälern, Pflegeheimen und ambulanten Diensten. iPersonal unterstützt Sie als spezialisierter Vermittler mit gezielter Jobplatzierung, persönlicher Beratung und direktem Zugang zu regionalen Arbeitgebern, was Ihnen einen reibungslosen Berufseinstieg oder Wechsel ermöglicht. Mit iPersonal profitieren Sie von umfassender Unterstützung und finden schneller die passende Stelle.

- Kostenlose Weiterbildungen über [Temptraining](https://temptraining.ch) – somit bekommt Ihre Karriere Rückenwind
- Eine feste Beraterin begleitet Sie persönlich, von der Bewerbung bis zum ersten Tag

description:

In unserem interdisziplinären Team aus Projektleiter:innen und Polygraf:innen mit Schwerpunkt Aktionswerbung und Preiskommunikation unterstützt du die Projektleiter:innen der Valencia Kommunikation AG in Basel. Ziel des sechsmonatigen Trainee\-Programms ist es, dich auf die Welt der Werbung vorzubereiten. Ein zentraler Bestandteil dabei ist das Kennenlernen der einzelnen Arbeitsschritte vom Briefing über die Umsetzung bis hin zur Produktion.  
Dein Weg in die operative Projektarbeit wird Schritt für Schritt aufgebaut und beginnt mit der selbstständigen Umsetzung kleinerer Projekte: Du erstellst Terminpläne und Offerten, briefst Teammitglieder, schreibst Rechnungen und stehst im Austausch mit Kund:innen sowie Dienstleister:innen. Da du in dieser Funktion viele Informationen liest, prüfst und vergleichst, sind eine hohe Konzentrationsfähigkeit, Genauigkeit sowie fokussiertes Arbeiten, auch über längere Zeit, besonders wichtig.  
Das Trainee\-Programm richtet sich an Talente mit organisatorischem Geschick, die Freude daran haben, vielfältige Aufgaben zu koordinieren. Fühlst du dich angesprochen? Dann erwartet dich ein praxisnahes Trainee\-Programm, das dir wertvolle Einblicke in die Arbeitswelt einer Kommunikationsagentur bietet.  
Das bringst du mit  
Persönlichkeit: Du bist aufgeschlossen, wissbegierig, anpassungsfähig, dienstleistungsorientiert und arbeitest gerne im Team.  
Arbeitsweise: Du arbeitest seriös, zuverlässig und behältst auch in hektischen Situationen den Überblick.  
Kommunikation: Du kommunizierst gerne, präzise und kannst vernetzt denken.  
Sprache und Text: Du hast Leidenschaft für Text, Wort und Schrift sowie Freude an Sprachen. Viele unserer Aufträge werden in Deutsch, ösisch und Italienisch umgesetzt. Du musst nicht alle Sprachen beherrschen, Grundkenntnisse sind aber hilfreich.  
Ausbildung: Du hast eine abgeschlossene Berufsbildung im kaufmännischen Bereich, einen eidg. Fachausweis als Kommunikations\-, PR\- oder Marketingfachfrau/\-mann, einen Fachhochschulabschluss im Bereich Marketing, Kommunikation oder Linguistik oder eine vergleichbare Ausbildung.  
Tools: Du bringst Anwendungskenntnisse in MS Office mit und hast Freude daran, weitere Software\-Programme zu erlernen.  
Warum Valencia?  
Weil du hier nicht einfach abarbeitest, sondern mitdenkst, mitgestaltest und Verantwortung übernimmst. Und weil wir überzeugt sind, dass gute Arbeit dort entsteht, wo Menschen Lust haben, sie gemeinsam gut zu machen.  
Dich erwarten die besten Arbeitskolleg:innen, vielseitige Projekte und ein zeitgemässes, flexibles Arbeitszeitmodell auf Basis einer 40‑Stunden\-Woche mit Remote\-Work\-Möglichkeit.  
Als monetäre Benefits erhältst du monatliche Lunchbons im Wert von CHF 150\.– und wir schenken dir nach der Probezeit das Halbtaxabonnement. Zusätzlich übernehmen wir deinen Krankentaggeldversicherungsbeitrag.  
Gleichzeitig investieren wir im Rahmen unserer «Academia de Valencia» bewusst in deine fachliche Entwicklung, sowohl zeitlich als auch finanziell.  
Du arbeitest in einer technisch hervorragend ausgestatteten Arbeitsumgebung mit flexiblen Arbeitsplätzen und schönen, offenen Räumen mitten in Basel. Unsere Agentur befindet sich in der Innenstadt und ist vom Bahnhof SBB in nur fünf Gehminuten erreichbar.  
Ein ganz besonderes Highlight ist unser jährlicher Agenturausflug: Gemeinsam verbringen wir ein Wochenende in «Valencia», wo auch immer dies sein mag.

title: Dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF/FH Tagdienst 50-100% für die Region Huttwil gesucht
description:
- Ein etabliertes Pflegeheim in der Region Huttwil sucht Verstärkung: Sie als Dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF/FH, geregelter Tagdienst mit planbaren Arbeitszeiten.

### Ihr Überblick zur Stelle als Dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF/FH in Huttwil

**Position:** Dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF/FH

**Fachbereich:** Tagdienst im Pflegeheim

**Pensum:** 50–100 % (flexibel wählbar)

**Anstellungsart:** Festanstellung

**Einsatzbeginn:** Ab sofort oder nach Vereinbarung

**Arbeitsort:** Region Huttwil

**Arbeitgeber:** Pflegeheim – den Namen erfahren Sie im Gespräch

Huttwil liegt im Emmental und besticht durch seine zentrale Lage in der Region Bern. Die gute Verkehrsanbindung mit Bahnverbindungen ermöglicht schnelle Pendelwege. Der Ort bietet attraktive Arbeitsbedingungen mit einem starken Handwerks- und Mittelstandssektor. Sie profitieren von der Nähe zur Natur, dem guten Arbeitsplatzangebot und erschwinglichen Lebenshaltungskosten.

### Das erwartet Sie als Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF/FH im Tagdienst in Huttwil

- Verantwortung für den gesamten Pflegeprozess von der Bedarfserhebung bis zur Auswertung
- Zudem: Durchführung ärztlicher Verordnungen sowie sichere Vorbereitung und Abgabe der Medikamente
- Überwachung von Vitalzeichen und frühzeitiges Erkennen von Zustandsveränderungen
- Fachliche Anleitung von FaGe, Pflegeassistenz und Lernenden im Team
- Ausserdem lückenlose Pflegedokumentation im elektronischen Pflegesystem
- Zusammenarbeit mit Ärzteschaft, Therapien und Angehörigen auf Augenhöhe
- Darüber hinaus Mitgestaltung von Pflegekonzepten sowie wir verbessern die Qualität stetig im Team
- Teilnahme an interprofessionellen Rapporten und Visiten im geregelten Tagdienst

### Ihr Profil – darauf kommt es an

- Abgeschlossene Ausbildung als dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF oder FH
- Bei ausländischem Diplom: SRK-Anerkennung zwingend erforderlich
- Zudem Erfahrung in der Langzeitpflege, Akutpflege oder Reha
- Vor allem hohes Verantwortungsbewusstsein, Empathie und Belastbarkeit
- Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift (mind. Niveau B2)

### Ihr Arbeitsumfeld: Tagdienst im Pflegeheim

Diese Stelle ist im Tagdienst angelegt. Sie arbeiten also in einer klaren Tagesstruktur mit geregelten Übergaben am Morgen und am Abend. Dabei nehmen Sie an Rapporten im Team mit Ärzten und Therapien teil, koordinieren Termine mit Ärzten und Therapeuten und begleiten Angehörigengespräche. Somit verbinden Sie fachliche Verantwortung mit einem planbaren Alltag.

- Sie tragen dabei die Verantwortung über den ganzen Pflegeprozess, von der Erhebung bis zur Auswertung

- Zuerst das Fachliche: die Ausbildung als dipl. Pflegefachfrau/-mann HF oder FH

Als diplomierte Pflegefachperson HF/FH tragen Sie die fachliche Verantwortung über den ganzen Pflegeprozess. Sie erheben den Pflegebedarf, danach planen Sie die Massnahmen und werten die Ergebnisse aus. Zudem steuern Sie die Abgabe der Medikamente, überwachen Vitalzeichen und erkennen Veränderungen früh. Somit entsteht Pflegequalität, die ankommt.

Der Weg in diesen Beruf führt über die höhere Fachschule (HF) oder das Bachelorstudium Pflege (FH). Ausländische Diplome brauchen dafür eine [Anerkennung durch das Schweizerische Rote Kreuz (SRK)](https://www.redcross.ch/de/srk-anerkennung). Ausserdem stehen erfahrenen Fachpersonen viele Wege offen: ein Nachdiplomstudium (NDS), die Rolle als Berufsbildnerin oder die Teamleitung.

title: Laboratory Manager
description:
The Quake Laboratory is being established at ETH Zürich in 2026 by Stephen Quake, who is moving from Stanford University. The lab works at the interface of physics, engineering, and biology, developing new measurement and modelling approaches that transform what is possible to learn from individual cells and from minute amounts of molecular material.

Three major research programmes will run in parallel: (1) reconstructing the regulatory architecture of E. coli at high resolution as a foundation for predictive models of gene regulation; (2) building large-scale single-cell atlases of human and model-organism tissues — including a first-of-its-kind atlas of the human autonomic nervous system — and training AI/foundation models on those atlases to interrogate aging biology and the evolution of multicellularity; and (3) advancing liquid-biopsy approaches that read cell-free nucleic acids from blood to detect disease, monitor physiology in collaboration with external partners.

The lab will be a multidisciplinary environment of approximately 10 people spanning molecular biologists, biochemists, computational biologists, machine-learning researchers, physicists, and engineers, with active collaborations across ETH, EPFL, the University of Zürich, and internationally.

The Laboratory Manager is the operational backbone of the group. You will own the day-to-day functioning of a complex, multi-modal wet lab — from bacterial molecular biology through human clinical sample processing through high-throughput sequencing — while serving as senior bench scientist, trainer, and trusted adviser to the PI on everything that keeps a productive research group running.

This role is ideal for an experienced research scientist who enjoys working across multiple biological systems, building infrastructure, mentoring less experienced colleagues, and taking pride in operational excellence. You will not be expected to drive a separate independent research programme; rather, you will enable and accelerate everyone else's. In return, you will be a core, named contributor on ambitious science, with a genuine voice in how the lab is built.

Lab operations and infrastructure

Lead the build-out and ongoing operation of the lab's wet-bench facilities at ETH, including equipment selection, installation, qualification, and routine maintenance contracts
Establish and maintain shared resources: cell culture rooms, BSL-2 areas, sequencing prep zones, –80 °C and liquid-nitrogen storage, autoclaves, common reagent stocks, and instrument calendars
Own ordering, supplier relationships, inventory management, and stockroom organisation across consumables and reagents; negotiate framework agreements where useful
Maintain and audit core SOPs, sample-tracking systems, and electronic lab notebook practices across the group
Serve as the lab's interface with ETH core facilities (e.g., Functional Genomics Center Zurich, ScopeM, Genome Engineering & Measurement Lab) and external service providers
Bacterial molecular biology and biochemistry — E. coli regulome

Run and oversee a molecular cloning pipeline for E. coli — design and assembly of plasmids and genome-integrated constructs, strain construction, and storage
Set up and maintain biochemical workflows relevant to regulatory studies: protein expression and purification, in vitro transcription, and quantitative biochemistry as projects require
Establish microbial growth, induction, and time-course infrastructure, including plate readers, continuous-culture systems, and microfluidics interfaces where relevant
Train new lab members in fundamental microbiology, sterile technique, and standard E. coli genetics; troubleshoot stuck cloning and expression projects
Mammalian cell biology and tissue handling — single-cell atlases

Run and supervise mammalian cell culture (primary cells, iPSC-derived cells, established lines), including media preparation, line authentication, and biobanking
Establish robust workflows for tissue dissociation, single-cell and single-nucleus suspension preparation, FACS-based cell sorting, and quality assessment
Coordinate the tissue-acquisition pipeline with clinical and academic partners — biospecimen agreements, chain-of-custody documentation, fixation and shipping logistics, ethics-approved sample handling
Liquid biopsy and cell-free nucleic acid workflows

Operate and maintain low-input cfDNA and cfRNA extraction workflows
Implement and refine cfNA library-preparation protocols (small-input WGS, methylation/EM-seq, fragmentomics, targeted panels, cfRNA-seq) and contribute to method development for new assay modalities
Establish quality-management practices appropriate to clinical-grade samples
High-throughput sequencing

Serve as the lab's senior practitioner for sequencing workflows— including library QC, pooling, balancing, and instrument operation or vendor coordination
Establish QC dashboards and acceptance criteria across library types (bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA/ATAC, spatial, cfDNA/cfRNA, microbial)
Coordinate with computational team members on sample sheets, demultiplexing, primary QC, and timely return of FASTQs and standard metrics
Maintain relationships with the Functional Genomics Center Zurich and external sequencing providers to handle overflow and specialty platforms
People, training, and culture

Onboard new lab members (postdocs, PhD and MSc students, technicians, visitors); design and deliver hands-on training in core methods
Mentor junior research staff and rotation students at the bench; lead routine technical lab meetings and troubleshooting clinics
Foster a rigorous, collaborative, and psychologically safe lab culture; embody and reinforce expectations around reproducibility, careful record-keeping, and intellectual honesty
Compliance, safety, and ethics

Serve as the lab's biosafety officer and primary point of contact for ETH Safety, Security, Health & Environment (SGU); maintain BSL-1/BSL-2 documentation, GMO and pathogen registrations as applicable
Ensure compliance with Swiss regulations on the use of human biological samples and personal data (Human Research Act, Federal Act on Data Protection), including ethics submissions and amendments
Manage chemical inventory, waste streams, radiation safety (where applicable), and animal-work documentation in coordination with ETH veterinary services
Lead the lab's emergency-preparedness procedures and serve as first responder for incidents
Desired Qualifications

Education: PhD in molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, genomics, or a closely related field; or a Master's degree with substantial additional research experience
Bench experience: At least 5 years of hands-on experience post-degree in a research lab, with demonstrable senior-level expertise across at least two of the three core areas (bacterial molecular biology / mammalian single-cell genomics / cell-free nucleic acid workflows)
Bacterial cloning and biochemistry: Independent experience designing and executing E. coli cloning, strain engineering, and protein biochemistry without supervision
Mammalian cell biology: Fluency in primary and cultured mammalian cell handling, FACS, and tissue dissociation for single-cell genomics
Sequencing: Direct experience preparing and QC'ing libraries for Illumina sequencing; familiarity with at least one long-read platform (ONT or PacBio) is a strong advantage
Liquid biopsy / cfNA: Demonstrated experience processing blood for cell-free nucleic acids and the pre-analytical care this requires
Lab leadership: Track record of training and supervising more junior scientists; ability to write clear SOPs and run a cross-functional bench operation
Operational competence: Comfortable with budgets, ordering systems, equipment service contracts, and biosafety documentation
Communication: Excellent written and spoken English; ability to interact effectively with clinicians, vendors, ETH administration, and external collaborators
Preferred Qualifications

Experience with single-cell genomics platforms (10x Genomics, Parse, Scale, Honeycomb) and spatial transcriptomics
Experience with clinical or biobank sample workflows under ISO 15189 / ISO 20387 or equivalent quality systems
Experience with Swiss research administration, ETH systems, or comparable European institutions
German language skills
A senior, intellectually central position in one of the most productive single-cell and measurement-science groups in the world as it moves from Stanford to ETH
Competitive ETH salary and benefits, commensurate with experience and ETH guidelines
A multi-year horizon: this is intended as a long-term role, not a stepping stone
Substantial influence on lab design, equipment selection, and operational standards
Co-authorship on publications you materially contribute to, in line with established practice
Professional development support, including conference travel and technical training

title: Export Compliance Engineer
description:
Join our team as an Export Compliance Engineer and combine your engineering expertise with international business, technology, and global trade affairs. You will work at the intersection of innovation, international trade, and regulatory compliance, supporting the worldwide delivery of advanced technologies while ensuring adherence to global export control requirements. This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy analyzing technical products and documentation, solving complex challenges, and collaborating with colleagues across engineering, project management, supply chain, and global operations. As part of our Trade Affairs organization, you will help ensure that cutting-edge technologies can be successfully and compliantly deployed around the world. **This is where you'll excel**
* You evaluate products, technologies, software, and technical data to determine export control classifications (ECN/ECCN) and licensing requirements * You review technical drawings, engineering documentation, product specifications, and technology transfers to ensure compliance with international export control regulations * You perform screenings, risk assessments, and end-use/end-user evaluations while supporting global customer projects from offer to delivery * You maintain export control records, classifications, licenses, and audit-ready documentation to ensure full regulatory compliance and traceability * You collaborate with engineering, project management, supply chain, and sales teams while driving process improvements, digitalization initiatives, and stakeholder training
**These are the skills you'll need**
* University degree in a technical discipline such as Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Automation Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a comparable field; additional knowledge of international trade or compliance is a plus * Strong analytical skills with the ability to understand and assess technical products, systems, drawings, and documentation * Independent, structured, and detail- and solution-oriented working style combined with strong cross-functional problem-solving capabilities * High level of responsibility, reliability, and integrity when dealing with complex technical and regulatory topics; experience with export control regulations or SAP GTS is advantageous * Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills with fluency in English; additional languages are a plus
**Attractive vacation entitlement** Enough time for relaxation and personal interests - we offer from 25 to 30 days of vacation per year depending on age. **Attractive mobility concept** We offer an OSTWIND ZVV / Z-Pass + half-fare travelcard for CHF 365 + CHF 400 public transport credit as well as an attractive first-class travelcard or free parking. **VIVA Restaurant** We offer our employees a daily fitness menu from 9, 00 CHF. **Employer-funded pension plan** The Bühler Pension Fund offers Bühler employees an independent pension fund that ensures reliable financial security in retirement: www.pk-buhler.ch **Health-Port** We are committed to preventive health care through laboratory analyses, massages, nutritional advice, physiotherapy, group courses and a company doctor. **Sports activities** We promote physical activity through self-organized circuit training and running groups as well as vouchers for Update and Activ Fitness. **Questions? We are happy to answer them!** Marcel Huber Senior Recruiting Specialist [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/marcel-huber-23a298b8/) **Creating impact together at Bühler!** Two billion people eat food every day that was produced with Bühler equipment. One billion people drive vehicles whose parts were manufactured with our machines. Bühler aims to balance humanity, nature, and the economy in every decision as it develops solutions that unlock sustainable business opportunities in the global food, feed, and mobility industries. We strive to create innovations for a better world, with a special focus on healthy, safe, and sustainable solutions. Therefore, we team up with customers, start-ups, multinationals, and academia to accelerate impact together.

un cadre de travail flexible et innovant

Brevet fédéral de spécialiste en ressources humaines ou formation supérieure jugée équivalente dans le domaine RH,

fortes qualités de coopération, d'éthique et d'intelligence relationnelle.

L’entreprise et vous  
Chez Services Plus Énergies (SPE), nous accompagnons nos clients dans les métiers du chauffage, de la ventilation et de la climatisation, avec une forte exigence de qualité, de réactivité et de fiabilité.

As a Specialist Neuroscience at Nestlé Research, your mission is to lead and contribute to research on the impact of nutrition in infant and child neurodevelopment through the concept, execution, and delivery of scientific projects for clinical substantiation You'll make a difference by collaborating closely with internal teams, external academic partners, laboratories, clinical research organizations, healthcare professionals and regulatory stakeholders. Head of Transportation Management  
We are looking for an experienced transportation professional to lead our chauffeur team while continuing to deliver exceptional service as a chauffeur. This role combines operational leadership with hands\-on client service and is ideal for someone who enjoys building efficient processes, developing people and ensuring an outstanding luxury client experience.  
Reporting to the Atrium’s Managing Director, you will coordinate the day\-to\-day operations of our transportation service, supervise a team of four chauffeurs, continuously improve departmental processes and ensure the highest standards of safety, reliability and professionalism are maintained across every client journey.

Team Leadership

Coach team members and promote a culture of professionalism, accountability and exceptional client service.

Transportation Operations

Develop, implement and continuously improve transportation procedures, standards and workflows.  
Ensure efficient route planning and optimal allocation of drivers and vehicles.  
Maintain operational documentation, SOPs and quality standards.

Ensure vehicles remain immaculate and presentation standards are consistently maintained.  
Maintain the highest level of confidentiality when dealing with clients and sensitive information.

Support other operational activities as required.

title: Thailändischer Spezialitäten Koch 100% (w/m/i)
description:
Eine Ikone der Schweizer Hotellerie und eine Legende seit der sensationellen Eröffnung im Jahr 1873. Gelegen auf dem Bürgenberg, einem 500 Meter hohen Felsvorsprung in der Zentralschweiz, zeichnet sich das Bürgenstock Resort Lake Lucerne durch gewagtes Design, bahnbrechende Nachhaltigkeit, atemberaubende Landschaften und modernste Freizeitangebote aus. Rund 700 Mitarbeitende aus 54 Nationen sorgen für exzellente Gastfreundschaft und bieten den perfekten Rahmen für Momente jenseits der Vorstellungskraft.

Drei exklusive Hotels, das Bürgenstock Hotel & Alpine Spa (5* Superior) mit den beiden Übernachtungsmöglichkeiten The Contemporary und The Heritage, das Waldhotel by Bürgenstock (5* Superior) und die Taverne 1879 (3*) stehen den Gästen zur Verfügung. Jedes dieser Häuser versteht es, eine einzigartige Atmosphäre zu kreieren. Zwölf Restaurants, Lounges und Bars sind das Schaufenster für kulinarische Exzellenz; im preisgekrönten Bürgenstock Alpine Spa und Waldhotel Spa finden Gäste die ultimative Entspannung. Das Resort ist nicht nur eine Traumdestination für Reisende aus aller Welt, sondern auch ein Arbeitsplatz mit hervorragender Unternehmenskultur.

Das Bürgenstock Resort erhielt das dritte Jahr in Folge die offizielle Zertifizierung als "Great Place to Work" der Schweiz – eine Auszeichnung, die das gesamte Team mit Stolz erfüllt.

Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir ab Dezember 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung eine/n:

Thailändischer Spezialitäten Koch 100% (w/m/i)

Zu Ihren Aufgaben gehören:
- das Sicherstellen eines authentischen & neuzeitlichen Speisenangebotes unter Berücksichtigung der Saisonprodukte des Originallandes sowie das Erstellen der Menükarte in Zusammenarbeit mit dem Corporate Culinary Director
- das Kreieren von neuen thailändischen Gerichten und Spezialitäten
- die Zubereitung der thailändischen Gerichte sowie der einwandfreie Umgang mit Produkten, Produktion- und Kochtechniken aus Thailand
- die Verantwortung der Einhaltung der Hygienerichtlinien sowie der Arbeitssicherheit
- das Kochen in der offenen Showküche vor dem Gast

Sie sind ein ausgebildeter Koch mit langjähriger Erfahrung sowie umfangreichem Fachwissen über die thailändische Spezialitätenküche sowie den fundierten thailändischen Kochtechniken. Sie haben Erfahrung in der internationalen gehobenen Gastronomie und Hotellerie. Deutsch und Englisch beherrschen Sie fließend, jede weitere Fremdsprache ist von Vorteil. Sie zeigen hohe Leistungsbereitschaft, sind leidenschaftlich und arbeiten auch unter Zeit- und Arbeitsdruck ruhig, exakt und gästeorientiert. Unternehmerisches Handeln und Denken zeichnet Sie aus.

Neben einem modernen Arbeitsplatz profitieren Sie von zahlreichen attraktiven Mitarbeiterangeboten und Vergünstigungen. Das Personalhaus verfügt über ein eigenes Fitnessstudio, eine TV-Lounge, einen Billardraum sowie eine Bibliothek. Darüber hinaus geniessen Sie Ermässigungen in unseren Restaurants sowie Vorzugskonditionen für Sie, Ihre Familie und Freunde für Übernachtungen in unseren Hotels. Weitere Vorteile umfassen Vergünstigungen für Tennis, Golf, Sportartikel, Versicherungen, Gruppenkurse und REKA-Checks.
Auch Ihre Mobilität unterstützen wir: Die Anreise mit öffentlichen Verkehrsmitteln wird finanziell gefördert, und Parkplätze stehen zu attraktiven Konditionen zur Verfügung.
Wir investieren in Ihre Zukunft: Mit Zugang zur Beekeeper-Mitarbeiterapp, vielfältigen Weiterbildungsangeboten, internen Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten und erstklassigen Karriereperspektiven schaffen wir den Rahmen für Ihre persönliche und berufliche Entfaltung.
Sie erwartet die Chance, Teil eines Weltklasse-Resorts zu sein, aktiv zum gemeinsamen Erfolg beizutragen und sich in einem inspirierenden Umfeld kontinuierlich weiterzuentwickeln.
Wir freuen uns auf Ihre vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen mit Motivationsschreiben, Arbeitszeugnissen und Foto.

title: Gestionnaire Contentieux & Faillites
description:
Gestionnaire Contentieux \& Faillites  
FER CIAM — L'humain au centre des prestations sociales  
La FER CIAM est l'agence genevoise de la plus grande caisse interprofessionnelle AVS de Suisse FER Genève, créée par la FER Genève et pleinement intégrée dans son écosystème de services aux entreprises membres.  
Avec près de 47'500 affiliés — entreprises et indépendants confondus — elle est l'un des acteurs incontournables de la protection sociale en Suisse romande.  
Au quotidien, ses équipes gèrent l'encaissement de 2,425 milliards de cotisations AVS et assurance chômage, ainsi que le versement de plus de 876 millions de francs de prestations AVS, AI et allocations perte de gain. En parallèle, elles assurent l'administration des allocations familiales et l'application des conventions collectives de travail.  
Un périmètre technique exigeant, au service de milliers d'entreprises et de leurs assurés — où chaque dossier a un impact direct sur la vie professionnelle et sociale des personnes concernées.  
Description du poste  
Votre mission :  
Au sein de la FER CIAM Genève, vous jouez un rôle clé dans la gestion et la sécurisation des créances des institutions affiliées. Vous pilotez les dossiers de contentieux, de poursuites et de faillites, assurez le suivi des procédures civiles et pénales ainsi que les actions en réparation du dommage, tout en accompagnant les affiliés et en collaborant étroitement avec les autorités et les partenaires internes. Votre rigueur et votre expertise permettent de garantir une gestion efficace des dossiers et la préservation des intérêts des institutions représentées.

Gestion des procédures de faillite

description:
Strategic Sourcing Manager - Forging & Casting

Purpose of the role:

  *  Developing and executing global sourcing strategies for the assigned direct materials categories: forging and casting
  *  Acting as a business partner to key stakeholders in business (Business Units, Engineering, etc.) and Operations (Product Line Supply Chain, Supplier Quality, Production, Materials Management, etc.).

  *  Application of aligned sourcing processes, sustainable supplier assessments and development approach, a performing and regulatory compliant supply base footprint shall be established and actively managed, contributing to the enhancement of the supply base performance on Quality, Delivery and Cost (QCD)
  *  Realization of a measurable value >3% in recurring and P&L effective cost reductions per year across the global 3rd party spend in the assigned spend categories accompanied by a leveraged and benchmarked supply base management
  *  Grow and further develop a qualified and performing Best Cost Country Supply Base in line with the companies and operations BCC objectives preferably in Eastern Europe and manage a sustainable spend allocation

  *  Accountable for contributing to the global Direct Material & Supply Base Performance (QCD)

  *  Providing forward-looking guidance on trends, threats and opportunities in own categories (eg. raw materials etc.)                          
  *  Active contribution to the bottom up alignment of the Direct Materials Category Team with the defined / set company objectives                                
  *  Interface to BU / Engineering for Strategic Sourcing activities along with the PDP (IP07) process

  *  Ensure consistent application of all Sourcing Levers
  *  Contribution to main Sourcing KPIs
  *  Assembles and actively leads category specific / cross-functional sourcing board

  *  Participates in and contributes to continuous improvement of direct material practices  


Qualifications:  

  *  5+ years in-depth strategic and operational sourcing experience with a solid working knowledge of global category management
  *  Demonstrated work experience on category specific production techniques and processes
  *  Knowledge about category sourcing markets

title: Laboratory Manager
description:
The Quake Laboratory is being established at ETH Zürich in 2026 by Stephen Quake, who is moving from Stanford University. The lab works at the interface of physics, engineering, and biology, developing new measurement and modelling approaches that transform what is possible to learn from individual cells and from minute amounts of molecular material.

Three major research programmes will run in parallel: (1) reconstructing the regulatory architecture of E. coli at high resolution as a foundation for predictive models of gene regulation; (2) building large-scale single-cell atlases of human and model-organism tissues — including a first-of-its-kind atlas of the human autonomic nervous system — and training AI/foundation models on those atlases to interrogate aging biology and the evolution of multicellularity; and (3) advancing liquid-biopsy approaches that read cell-free nucleic acids from blood to detect disease, monitor physiology in collaboration with external partners.

The lab will be a multidisciplinary environment of approximately 10 people spanning molecular biologists, biochemists, computational biologists, machine-learning researchers, physicists, and engineers, with active collaborations across ETH, EPFL, the University of Zürich, and internationally.

The Laboratory Manager is the operational backbone of the group. You will own the day-to-day functioning of a complex, multi-modal wet lab — from bacterial molecular biology through human clinical sample processing through high-throughput sequencing — while serving as senior bench scientist, trainer, and trusted adviser to the PI on everything that keeps a productive research group running.

This role is ideal for an experienced research scientist who enjoys working across multiple biological systems, building infrastructure, mentoring less experienced colleagues, and taking pride in operational excellence. You will not be expected to drive a separate independent research programme; rather, you will enable and accelerate everyone else's. In return, you will be a core, named contributor on ambitious science, with a genuine voice in how the lab is built.

Lab operations and infrastructure

Lead the build-out and ongoing operation of the lab's wet-bench facilities at ETH, including equipment selection, installation, qualification, and routine maintenance contracts
Establish and maintain shared resources: cell culture rooms, BSL-2 areas, sequencing prep zones, –80 °C and liquid-nitrogen storage, autoclaves, common reagent stocks, and instrument calendars
Own ordering, supplier relationships, inventory management, and stockroom organisation across consumables and reagents; negotiate framework agreements where useful
Maintain and audit core SOPs, sample-tracking systems, and electronic lab notebook practices across the group
Serve as the lab's interface with ETH core facilities (e.g., Functional Genomics Center Zurich, ScopeM, Genome Engineering & Measurement Lab) and external service providers
Bacterial molecular biology and biochemistry — E. coli regulome

Run and oversee a molecular cloning pipeline for E. coli — design and assembly of plasmids and genome-integrated constructs, strain construction, and storage
Set up and maintain biochemical workflows relevant to regulatory studies: protein expression and purification, in vitro transcription, and quantitative biochemistry as projects require
Establish microbial growth, induction, and time-course infrastructure, including plate readers, continuous-culture systems, and microfluidics interfaces where relevant
Train new lab members in fundamental microbiology, sterile technique, and standard E. coli genetics; troubleshoot stuck cloning and expression projects
Mammalian cell biology and tissue handling — single-cell atlases

Run and supervise mammalian cell culture (primary cells, iPSC-derived cells, established lines), including media preparation, line authentication, and biobanking
Establish robust workflows for tissue dissociation, single-cell and single-nucleus suspension preparation, FACS-based cell sorting, and quality assessment
Coordinate the tissue-acquisition pipeline with clinical and academic partners — biospecimen agreements, chain-of-custody documentation, fixation and shipping logistics, ethics-approved sample handling
Liquid biopsy and cell-free nucleic acid workflows

Operate and maintain low-input cfDNA and cfRNA extraction workflows
Implement and refine cfNA library-preparation protocols (small-input WGS, methylation/EM-seq, fragmentomics, targeted panels, cfRNA-seq) and contribute to method development for new assay modalities
Establish quality-management practices appropriate to clinical-grade samples
High-throughput sequencing

Serve as the lab's senior practitioner for sequencing workflows— including library QC, pooling, balancing, and instrument operation or vendor coordination
Establish QC dashboards and acceptance criteria across library types (bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA/ATAC, spatial, cfDNA/cfRNA, microbial)
Coordinate with computational team members on sample sheets, demultiplexing, primary QC, and timely return of FASTQs and standard metrics
Maintain relationships with the Functional Genomics Center Zurich and external sequencing providers to handle overflow and specialty platforms
People, training, and culture

Onboard new lab members (postdocs, PhD and MSc students, technicians, visitors); design and deliver hands-on training in core methods
Mentor junior research staff and rotation students at the bench; lead routine technical lab meetings and troubleshooting clinics
Foster a rigorous, collaborative, and psychologically safe lab culture; embody and reinforce expectations around reproducibility, careful record-keeping, and intellectual honesty
Compliance, safety, and ethics

Serve as the lab's biosafety officer and primary point of contact for ETH Safety, Security, Health & Environment (SGU); maintain BSL-1/BSL-2 documentation, GMO and pathogen registrations as applicable
Ensure compliance with Swiss regulations on the use of human biological samples and personal data (Human Research Act, Federal Act on Data Protection), including ethics submissions and amendments
Manage chemical inventory, waste streams, radiation safety (where applicable), and animal-work documentation in coordination with ETH veterinary services
Lead the lab's emergency-preparedness procedures and serve as first responder for incidents
Desired Qualifications

Education: PhD in molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, genomics, or a closely related field; or a Master's degree with substantial additional research experience
Bench experience: At least 5 years of hands-on experience post-degree in a research lab, with demonstrable senior-level expertise across at least two of the three core areas (bacterial molecular biology / mammalian single-cell genomics / cell-free nucleic acid workflows)
Bacterial cloning and biochemistry: Independent experience designing and executing E. coli cloning, strain engineering, and protein biochemistry without supervision
Mammalian cell biology: Fluency in primary and cultured mammalian cell handling, FACS, and tissue dissociation for single-cell genomics
Sequencing: Direct experience preparing and QC'ing libraries for Illumina sequencing; familiarity with at least one long-read platform (ONT or PacBio) is a strong advantage
Liquid biopsy / cfNA: Demonstrated experience processing blood for cell-free nucleic acids and the pre-analytical care this requires
Lab leadership: Track record of training and supervising more junior scientists; ability to write clear SOPs and run a cross-functional bench operation
Operational competence: Comfortable with budgets, ordering systems, equipment service contracts, and biosafety documentation
Communication: Excellent written and spoken English; ability to interact effectively with clinicians, vendors, ETH administration, and external collaborators
Preferred Qualifications

Experience with single-cell genomics platforms (10x Genomics, Parse, Scale, Honeycomb) and spatial transcriptomics
Experience with clinical or biobank sample workflows under ISO 15189 / ISO 20387 or equivalent quality systems
Experience with Swiss research administration, ETH systems, or comparable European institutions
German language skills
A senior, intellectually central position in one of the most productive single-cell and measurement-science groups in the world as it moves from Stanford to ETH
Competitive ETH salary and benefits, commensurate with experience and ETH guidelines
A multi-year horizon: this is intended as a long-term role, not a stepping stone
Substantial influence on lab design, equipment selection, and operational standards
Co-authorship on publications you materially contribute to, in line with established practice
Professional development support, including conference travel and technical training
Relocation support for candidates moving to Basel, in line with E

title: Director of Expeditions
description:
Director of Expeditions - School in Switzerland

A prestigious and internationally renowned boarding school in Switzerland is seeking an outstanding Director of Expeditions to lead one of the most distinctive outdoor education programmes in the world. Reporting to a senior member of the leadership team, the successful candidate will provide strategic and operational leadership for a large-scale expedition programme encompassing mountain, ski and adventure-based learning experiences. This is a rare opportunity for an experienced outdoor education professional with strong leadership credentials, technical expertise in alpine environments and a passion for developing young people through challenge, resilience and discovery.

JOB PURPOSE
The Director of Expeditions serves as the strategic lead for Aiglon’s renowned expedition department. The post holder is responsible for the development and delivery of the programme’s vision and ethos, ensuring it is progressive, relevant, and distilled into a coherent curriculum across the whole school. They provide leadership to a team of qualified expeditioners and ensure that all activities are managed with the highest standards of safety and risk management.
KEY TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THE POSITION

1. Strategic Leadership & Vision

Visionary Design: Develop and oversee the philosophy and approach of our expedition programme, ensuring it reflects our aim to continue to be world leading in outdoor pursuit provision.
Curriculum Development: Develop and implement the expedition programme ensuring it is progressive for all students, regardless of age or length of stay at Aiglon.
Challenge: Ensure challenge is appropriate to ability and context, acknowledging that expeditions serve pastoral and community-building purposes alongside physical stretch.
Reinforce the purpose of expeditions: independence, resilience, responsibility and growth.
Holistic Assessment: Take a lead role in the school’s development of holistic assessment within the expedition context.
External Engagement: Seek to build relationships with the wider community to share expertise and gain insights from external best practices, with particular emphasis on risk management.

2. Operational Oversight & Management
Team Leadership: Provide instruction and guidance to the Head of Senior and Junior Expeditions in their operational oversight.
Leadership: Provide inspiration, leadership and guidance to all teaching staff involved in expeditions with the expectation to deliver the highest standards and professionalism.
Staff Development: Manage professional reviews, appraisals, and training (internal and external) for the expedition staff.
Meetings: Chair expedition department meetings and work closely with both Junior and Senior heads to ensure departmental alignment.
Stakeholder Liaison: Liaise with the School Council, Assistant Heads, Houseparents, and academic departments.
Recruitment: Oversee and support the recruitment of all expedition staff, including guides.
Development: Monitor and continually improve the process of student reflection.
Administration: Ensure all paperwork and communication is complete, efficient and effective.
Budgets: Preparation and management of all Expedition budgets
Administration: Use Aiglon’s data management system to record and organise all expeditions
Mountain School: Line-manage the Junior Mountain School Programme, with specific liaison with the Bear Grylls Survival Academy
Summer Camp: Act as the senior advisor for all summer expedition activities, ensuring a robust handover of safety protocols and operational standards to the Summer School team while maintaining ultimate accountability for safeguarding and risk management frameworks.
3. Safety, Risk & Compliance
Safety Evaluation: Oversee and evaluate the safety protocols of the entire expedition programme.
Risk Management: Encourage and verify a high level of risk management documentation and ensure operating standards align with best practice.
Open Culture: Ensure a safe and open environment for staff to share experiences and opinions to improve safety.
Compliance: Ensure that all equipment and its usage comply with current PPE and safety standards.
Work closely with the HR team and Director of Compliance to ensure compliance with all necessary processes relating to recruitment of guides.
Ensure that qualifications of all staff and Guides are appropriate.
Safeguarding: Ensure all staff and Guides receive safeguarding training at regular intervals. There is an expectation to uphold the highest standards of safeguarding.

4. Logistics & Equipment Management
Planning & Bookings: Oversee and guide administrative support and the Heads of Expeditions to ensure bookings are made with a nine to twelve-month lead-in.
Stores Management: Manage the expedition stores, including the upkeep, care, and long-term planning for equipment.
Inventory Systems: Manage robust systems for recording inventories and maintenance schedules.
5. Communication & Ethos
Internal Communication: Ensure students, staff and parents receive effective and efficient information regarding upcoming expeditions through assemblies, staff meetings, bulletins and external communication.
External Communication: Work with communications, admissions, and advancement teams to ensure clear and inspiring messaging to the wider community, that is delivered to a high professional standard..
Institutional Values: Contribute enthusiastically to the life and work of the school, upholding the Aiglon ethos, including the delivery of meditations.
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
The Director of Expeditions is expected to be visible and motivational presence and contribute to the overall life of the Aiglon community
Undertake additional responsibilities as may arise at the reasonable request of the Director of Character Education and the Director of School.

The qualifications, experiences and attributes of the post holder must match the detailed specification below:
A. Education, Qualifications and Languages
Essential

Swiss-recognised International Mountain Leader/Accompagnateur
Winter mountaineering or ski qualification
Rock Climbing Instructor
First Aid certification
Driving licence
Professional working proficiency in French and a fluency in English

Desirable

Teaching qualification
Holder of an IFGMA qualification
Higher level qualification in other adventure activities:
Paddlesports
Mountain Biking

B. Experience and Knowledge
Essential

Experience in health and safety auditing, incident management protocols, and Swiss legal requirements for high-risk activities.
Experience in managing department budgets, equipment procurement, and overseeing a team of full-time and freelance staff.
Experience in designing progressive outdoor education programs that align with educational frameworks
Experience leading and teaching young people and groups in the European mountains in a variety of adventurous activities
Highly competent skier
Professional-level competence in winter navigation and avalanche safety
Experience in the creation and delivery of presentations and information to a wide range of audiences

C. Personal Qualities, Attitudes and Behaviours
Essential

Ability to build professional relationships with students within the clear boundaries of Aiglon’s safeguarding policies.
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively across all stakeholders.
The ability to inspire confidence in staff, students and parents whilst articulating the value of risk to the School Council and Board of Directors.
Proven ability to remain calm and lead a team through high-pressure emergency situations in remote environments.
Aiglon expects the Director to have a commitment to continuous professional development, staying at the forefront of international outdoor education trends and safety standards; they should also be expected to mentor junior staff in their professional development.

title: Observability Engineer
description:
Observability Engineer  
Job Description  
As an Observability Engineer, you will take on hands\-on engineering role with real influence on the evolution of our observability landscape. You design, implement and operate modern observability solutions that ensure transparency, reliability and performance of our IT services across cloud and on\-premises environments.  
This role combines deep technical ownership with exposure to modern observability standards and cloud technologies. You will work closely with experienced platform, architecture and service management teams and collaborate with our ServiceNow team to technically integrate observability signals and alerts into Service Now Event Management (ITOM).  
While your focus remains hands\-on engineering, platform operation, and continuous improvement, you will also actively contribute to strategic topics such as observability strategy, roadmap definition and platform evolution, while remaining strongly rooted in implementation and day\-to\-day operations.  
Engineer, operate and continuously improve observability platforms as a service for infrastructure, platform and application teams;  
Implement and maintain telemetry collection for metrics, logs and traces using open standards such as Prometheus and OpenTelemetry;  
Design and operate scalable telemetry pipelines, including collection, processing, enrichment and routing of observability data;  
Build and maintain dashboards, alerts and service level indicators that support both operational teams and service owners;  
Integrate observability platforms with IT service management solutions, event management, and automation workflows;  
Support migration from legacy monitoring platforms to modern observability solutions;  
Troubleshoot complex performance and availability issues across distributed systems;  
Collaborate closely with application teams, service owners and platform stakeholders, providing consultative guidance and observability best practices to improve observability coverage and signal quality;  
Contribute to the definition and evolution of observability standards, best practices and guidelines;  
Contribute input to observability strategy, roadmap planning and technology evaluation;  
Create and maintain operational documentation, runbooks, and onboarding guides.  
Requirements  
Proven hands\-on experience as an Observability Engineer, Monitoring Engineer or similar technical role;  
Practical experience with open standards and ecosystems such as Prometheus, OpenTelemetry and related tooling;  
Experience designing and operating telemetry pipelines for metrics, logs, and traces;  
Experience with observability in modern distributed systems and cloud native architectures;  
Experience with LLM observability, including monitoring, tracing, and quality signals for AI or ML based workloads;  
Experience migrating from existing monitoring platforms to new observability platforms is a strong plus;  
Experience with cloud platforms, especially Microsoft Azure;  
Experience with on\-premises environments, particularly Microsoft based virtualized infrastructures;  
Experience with scripting and automation using tools such as PowerShell, Bash, JSON or YAML;  
Experience deploying Observability solutions / platform as IaC (Terraform);  
Good understanding of IT service management processes and event driven operations is a plus;  
Strong problem\-solving skills and a structured, analytical mindset;  
Ability to collaborate effectively across infrastructure, platform, application and architecture teams;  
Proactive mindset with a strong willingness to learn and continuously improve;  
Fluent English verbal and written communication skills. German is a plus.  
What you can expect  
We provide modern working conditions, including work\-from\-home options, flexible hours and a home office allowance to ensure staff members have a work environment equipped with the latest technology;  
A diverse culture founded on mutual respect, teamwork and appreciation awaits you at LGT Capital Partners. We go the extra mile to generate impact;  
We empower and invest in you: your professional development and personal growth are our priority. We offer various internal and external training opportunities that are aligned with your ambitions and our business needs. If you are interested, you can also enhance your German or English language skills  
We are proud to be owned by the Princely Family of Liechtenstein and our company is inspired by its entrepreneurial spirit;  
Commitment to ESG: our approach to business is influenced by the Princely Family's long\-term perspective. Sustainability is key for us and has shaped our actions since 2002;  
You benefit from favorable terms and conditions if you wish to participate in LGT Capital Partners' investment programs or to use LGT banking products and services.

For further information please contact us.

title: Strategic Sourcing Manager - Forging & Casting
description:
Strategic Sourcing Manager - Forging & Casting

Purpose of the role:

  *  Developing and executing global sourcing strategies for the assigned direct materials categories: forging and casting
  *  Acting as a business partner to key stakeholders in business (Business Units, Engineering, etc.) and Operations (Product Line Supply Chain, Supplier Quality, Production, Materials Management, etc.).
  *  The global category manager shall sustain the Global Strategic Sourcing Operating Model and provide the supply capability and capacity at best cost to support the company’s future business needs and protection of brand value
  *  Application of aligned sourcing processes, sustainable supplier assessments and development approach, a performing and regulatory compliant supply base footprint shall be established and actively managed, contributing to the enhancement of the supply base performance on Quality, Delivery and Cost (QCD)
  *  Realization of a measurable value >3% in recurring and P&L effective cost reductions per year across the global 3rd party spend in the assigned spend categories accompanied by a leveraged and benchmarked supply base management
  *  Grow and further develop a qualified and performing Best Cost Country Supply Base in line with the companies and operations BCC objectives preferably in Eastern Europe and manage a sustainable spend allocation


Responsibilities:

  *  Management of own material categories (capacity, knowledge management, performance)                
  *  Accountable for contributing to the global Direct Material & Supply Base Performance (QCD)        
  *  Representing own direct material categories within the VAT organization                              
  *  Accountable for the category specific achievement of the objectives of cost optimization, supply base optimization, geographic sourcing footprint and Best Cost Country Sourcing                          
  *  Providing forward-looking guidance on trends, threats and opportunities in own categories (eg. raw materials etc.)                          
  *  Active contribution to the bottom up alignment of the Direct Materials Category Team with the defined / set company objectives                                
  *  Interface to BU / Engineering for Strategic Sourcing activities along with the PDP (IP07) process  
  *  Act as a change agent in regards to main stakeholders
  *  Perform the development of category sourcing strategies applying and complying with defined methods and tools
  *  Active supplier relationship management of the global supply base within its own category perimeter in alignment with the category teams in Switzerland, Malaysia and Romania
  *  Ensure consistent application of all Sourcing Levers
  *  Contribution to main Sourcing KPIs
  *  Assembles and actively leads category specific / cross-functional sourcing board
  *  Actively monitors and performs a supply base risk assessment across its own categories
  *  Participates in and contributes to continuous improvement of direct material practices  


Qualifications:  

  *  5+ years in-depth strategic and operational sourcing experience with a solid working knowledge of global category management
  *  Demonstrated work experience on category specific production techniques and processes
  *  Knowledge about category sourcing markets
  *  Office Software / IT application (esp. Excel, Word, Power Point etc.)
  *  Sourcing in Eastern Europe, Asia and experience in Best Cost Country and spend relocation activities
  *  Working experience within a global complex organization
  *  Experience in the field of machine building, vacuum technology and semiconductors
  *  Cross-function / category team management (min. functional)
  *  Sensible and emphatic communication skills with suppliers, colleagues, internal stakeholders, etc.
  *  Strong analytical skills (risk based) and focus on the essential facts
  *  Able to get results through others, able to multi-task, sense of priority, able to handle stress levels
  *  Good communication skills in German and English (any other language will be a plus)

title: Director, Global Commodity Management & Analytics
description:
Ready to make your next big professional move? Join us on our journey to achieve our big dream of building the most loved restaurant brands in the world.  

Restaurant Brands International Inc. is one of the world's largest quick service restaurant companies with nearly $45 billion in annual system-wide sales and over 32,000 restaurants in more than 120 countries and territories.

RBI owns four of the world's most prominent and iconic quick service restaurant brands – TIM HORTONS®, BURGER KING®, POPEYES®, and FIREHOUSE SUBS®. These independently operated brands have been serving their respective guests, franchisees and communities for decades. Through its Restaurant Brands for Good framework, RBI is improving sustainable outcomes related to its food, the planet, and people and communities.

RBI is committed to growing the TIM HORTONS®, BURGER KING®, POPEYES® and FIREHOUSE SUBS® brands by leveraging their respective core values, employee and franchisee relationships, and long track records of community support. Each brand benefits from the global scale and shared best practices that come from ownership by Restaurant Brands International Inc.

RBI’s Global Commodities & Intelligence Centre of Excellence

RBI is strengthening its global procurement organization by establishing a Global Commodities & Intelligence Centre of Excellence (CoE).

The CoE will provide commodity intelligence, data, risk management, and commercial decision support to procurement teams across RBI’s brands and markets. It will act as the analytical backbone of the global procurement function, helping regional teams make faster, data-driven sourcing and negotiation decisions.

Our Opportunity:

The Director, Global Commodity Management & Analytics will build and lead RBI’s newly established CoE, including its operating model, governance, analytical capabilities, tools, and team.

This is a newly created global role for a commercially minded commodity leader with deep market expertise, strong negotiation experience, advanced analytical capabilities, and an interest in using AI and data to improve procurement decisions.

The role will focus primarily on the following direct commodity categories:

Sugar, Wheat, Soy, Corn, Pork, Beef, Chicken, Paperboard, and Potatoes

The CoE will own market intelligence, forecasting, cost modelling, risk management, sourcing strategy, and upstream commercial negotiations for these categories, depending on the market.

The role will also provide advisory intelligence and risk support for selected indirect categories, including metals, steel, engineering, energy, maintenance, repair and operations, and industrial gases.

The CoE will lead or support negotiations for upstream raw materials, including raw meat cuts, agricultural commodities, and packaging feedstocks.

RBI follows a five-day, in-office work schedule to support collaboration. Candidates should be comfortable working onsite five days per week.

Your Roles & Responsibilities:

Build and lead the Global Commodities & Intelligence CoE, establishing its operating model, governance, team structure, priorities, and ways of working with regional and global procurement teams.
Define RBI’s global commodity intelligence strategy, including frameworks for market monitoring, price forecasting, risk assessment, scenario planning, and procurement timing recommendations.
Develop and deploy AI-enabled intelligence capabilities, including forecasting models, real-time market monitoring, should-cost tools, scenario analysis, and executive risk dashboards.
Own RBI’s global commodity risk management strategy, covering forward contracting, index-linked pricing, supplier diversification, pooling opportunities, hedging considerations, and spot, forward, and long-term supply arrangements.
Lead upstream commodity negotiations across the direct category portfolio, from market analysis and strategy development through to supplier engagement and commercial execution, as appropriate by market.
Lead RBI’s Global Contingency and Risk Management Programme, including supply-chain stress testing, inventory and business-continuity planning, geopolitical and weather-risk analysis, reporting, and executive escalation.
Establish global should-cost models, cost benchmarks, and pricing mechanisms that help procurement teams validate supplier proposals and strengthen sourcing and negotiation decisions.
Manage external commodity consultancies, market-data providers, and intelligence platforms, while building an integrated and scalable data infrastructure across markets and functions.
Act as RBI’s global commodity intelligence leader, delivering market outlooks, cost-impact analysis, sourcing recommendations, and executive briefings to senior procurement, finance, and brand leaders.
Partner with Procurement, Finance, Treasury, Supply Chain, Operations, R&D, Quality Assurance, Sustainability, and Brand teams to deliver cost savings, cost avoidance, supply resilience, responsible sourcing, and stronger procurement governance.

Your skills & experience:

10+ years of progressive experience in global commodity procurement, trading, supply chain risk management, or commodity market intelligence within a large-scale FMCG, food service, QSR, or agri-food business.
Demonstrable expertise across at least three of the nine Direct categories; proven track record of executing upstream raw commodity negotiations at significant scale, including proteins (Beef, Chicken, Pork), grains, oilseeds, or packaging feedstocks.
Strong working knowledge of commodity markets, exchange mechanics (CME, CBOT, ICE), financial risk instruments (futures, options, swaps), and price risk management frameworks.
Proven experience deploying or commissioning AI, machine learning, or advanced analytics tools for commodity forecasting, market monitoring, or procurement decision support.
Experience building or leading a Centre of Excellence, intelligence function, or data capability within a complex global organization.
Track record of managing external consultancies, market data vendors, and analytics platform relationships at enterprise scale.
Experience operating within global matrixed organizations with multiple brands, procurement cooperatives, or franchise networks; able to influence without direct authority across regional structures.
Strong commercial acumen with the ability to translate commodity market dynamics into clear business recommendations and financial impact models.
Excellent communicator and executive presence; comfortable presenting to C-suite and Board-level audiences.
Fluent in English; additional languages (French, German, Spanish, Portuguese) are an asset.

We are looking for:

A seasoned commodity professional who can build and lead a high-impact global intelligence function while also owning the commercial execution of RBI’s upstream raw commodity portfolio. You operate at the intersection of markets, data, and strategy. You are as comfortable at the negotiating table as you are presenting a risk scenario to the Board. You influence regional teams through the quality of your intelligence and the rigor of your commercial outcomes. You are energized by complexity, clarity, and building things that others depend on.

title: Clinical Development Lead
description:
Are you an experienced clinical development professional eager to take scientific ownership of a clinical program and help shape the future of a differentiated therapy?

We are seeking a scientifically curious, strategic and hands-on Clinical Development Lead to provide clinical and scientific leadership across the design, execution and interpretation of clinical studies. In this role, you will play a central role in translating scientific insight into high-quality clinical evidence and development decisions that can make a meaningful difference for patients.

This role offers the opportunity to shape lifecycle evidence generation and unlock the full potential of differentiated medicines through clinically meaningful, scientifically robust and strategically aligned development activities.

Working closely with Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Drug Safety, Biostatistics, Medical Affairs and Commercial colleagues, you will ensure development plans are scientifically robust, operationally feasible and strategically aligned. This is an opportunity to combine scientific depth with visible cross-functional leadership in an entrepreneurial, collaborative and fast-moving environment.

Key Responsibilities

The Clinical Development Lead is the clinical and scientific expert responsible for leading the delivery of clinical program objectives for an assigned compound, in line with Company strategy and agreed development plans.

Main responsibilities include:

•    Lead the multidisciplinary Clinical Team at development-program level, providing scientific direction, strategic alignment and accountability across the program.
•    Shape innovative clinical development strategies that maximize the compound's value throughout its lifecycle, integrating emerging scientific evidence and evolving standard of care into development plans.
•    Lead the scientific development and delivery of clinical sections of trial- and program-level regulatory documents, including Investigator’s Brochures, briefing books, safety updates, submission dossiers and responses to Health Authorities.
•    Provide thought leadership in clinical trial design and execution in close partnership with key functions, ensuring scientific quality, clear prioritisation and timely delivery.
•    Provide ongoing clinical and scientific review, interpretation and communication of clinical trial data to inform program strategy and development decisions.
•    Serve as a core member of the Safety Management Team and contribute to the assessment and communication of the compound’s benefit-risk profile.
•    Support the preparation of safety-related documents, including Periodic Safety Update Reports, Drug Safety Update Reports and other safety documentation, in collaboration with the Project Physician and Drug Safety Physician.
•    Maintain a strong understanding of the therapeutic area, competitive landscape, relevant mechanisms of action and evolving standards of care.
•    Lead clinical contributions to scientific communications, including study abstracts, posters, oral presentations and manuscripts.
•    Represent the Company as a credible scientific leader externally with investigators, scientific experts, advisory boards and Health Authorities.
•    Champion the clinical perspective in cross-functional discussions and support the continuous evolution of the clinical development strategy.

Candidate Requirements

•    Advanced degree in life or health sciences, such as PhD, MD, PharmD, MSc or equivalent.
•    At least eight years of relevant experience in clinical development within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
•    Proven experience leading Phase II to IV clinical development programs in global, cross-functional matrix environments through successful planning, delivery and publication.
•    Strong experience supporting global regulatory submissions and Health Authority interactions, including the preparation of key clinical and regulatory documents throughout the development lifecycle.
•    Excellent understanding of global drug development and innovative clinical trial design through all phases, with the ability to integrate preclinical, translational, clinical, and real-world evidence to inform development strategies; pediatric development experience is an advantage.
•    Intellectually curious with strong scientific acumen, entrepreneurial spirit, and learning agility, with the ability to challenge conventional thinking constructively.
•    Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong executive presence and the ability to effectively communicate complex scientific concepts to diverse internal and external stakeholders
•    Strong project management, prioritization, problem-solving and stakeholder-management capabilities.
•    Ability to work independently, influence decision-making and build alignment across cross-functional teams in a dynamic matrix organization.
•    A collaborative, proactive and pragmatic mindset, with a strong sense of ownership and commitment to delivering high-quality clinical evidence.
